value.rules_markdown:
- Each module has one responsibility, with core types in a module-local types.rs.
- Every port in src/ports/ is one trait in one file.
- Declare every CLI subcommand even when its milestone has not landed, for a stable surface.
- src/server/ is the only production surface; do not distribute or run as a GitHub Action.
- Put anything needing model or write credentials in src/server/, not in a workflow.
- Presets are data in folders with preset.toml and README.md; adding a preset is a new folder, never a new module.
- Vendor/tinyagents is a git submodule; never edit it here, change it upstream and bump the pin.
- Declare examples explicitly in Cargo.toml with required-features so credential-needing smoke tests never build in CI.
- Keep the default build offline; put anything needing the network behind a feature (harness, github, serve).
- Use rustfmt output and Rust 2024 idioms; snake_case modules/files, PascalCase types.
- Return Result<T> using the crate error type from src/error.rs.
- Start every file with a //! module doc describing its role and any feature gating.
- Comments explain the decision, not the code; flag load-bearing orderings and state why.
- Public items carry doc comments; Clap fields use /// so it becomes help text.
- Tests live in-crate as #[cfg(test)] mod tests at module bottom, moving to sibling test.rs when they grow; no tests/ directory.
- Every port has an always-compiled offline mock; MockForge records what would have been written.
- Cover lane behaviour with golden tests asserting findings that survive filtering, dedupe and capping.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- Keep every Markdown file at 500 lines or fewer; split and link from the module's README.md when larger.
- The model never holds a write token; write credentials are minted only in src/apply/ after all model calls return.
- Never execute contributor code; only read the diff and tree.
- Treat PR bodies, comments and diffs as untrusted input; fence and label them as data in prompts.
- Only deterministic policy in src/apply/ and src/automerge/ may mutate GitHub; model verdicts are advisory.
- Report found secrets by type and location only; the value never reaches comments, summaries, or logs.
- Use concise imperative commit subjects; keep commits small and each coherent validated slice separate.
- Pull requests state what changed, any behaviour change, and how it was verified.
